item.title: Last-second 3-pointer sends RC to rare 1st-round exit
item.description: For the first time in 10 years, Ripon Christian has been eliminated in the first round of the Sac-Joaquin Section playoffs. While the Knights may be lamenting some missed opportunities from their Division IV opener on Wednesday, ninth-seeded Union Mine is likely still buzzing after stealing a 63-62 win thanks to a couple big-time makes on broken plays in the final minute.

item.title: Knights advance to 3rd consecutive SJS final
item.description: Top-seeded Ripon Christian took 13 first-half shots Wednesday night against visiting No. 5 Vacaville Christian and had just one goal to show for it. Coach David Morris got the Knights headed in the right direction in the second half, with Kylie Koolhaas finding the goal in less than a minute after coming out of the locker room.

item.title: EU nets 1st home playoff win since 2004
item.description: The East Union Lancers had three players score at least 15 points, played suffocating defense and dominated Nevada Union on the boards on the way to a 66-50 victory in the opening round of the Sac-Joaquin Section III playoffs Wednesday night. It’s the program’s first home playoff win since 2004.

item.title: Horror of horrors: Dave Breitenbucher drinks Manteca city tap water & has even done so from a garden hose
item.description: Dave Breitenbucher is a 63 year-old “grandpa” who indulges his grandkids by bouncing around with them at Altitude Trampoline Park on Spreckels Avenue.

item.title: RAIN, COLD IMPERIL ALMONDS
item.description: Continued rain with wind almost daily through March 2 with only a handful of days where the highs will get past the mid-60s could dampen prospects for the 2026 almond crop.

item.title: Dueling Pianos featuring MHS grad plays Deaf Puppy for 2 days
item.description: Deaf Puppy is bringing back the Dueling Pianos this Friday and Saturday.

item.title: Two-way Zoom public comments coming to Manteca council meetings
item.description: Those commenting during Manteca City Council meetings after July 1 will be seen as well as heard.

item.title: Some see crackdown on rogue behavior as being anti-bicycling
item.description: Social media criticism about a pending crackdown on organized or spontaneous street takeovers by bicyclist prompted measured pushback from the Manteca City Council on Tuesday.

item.title: 24 apartments previously approved for Airport Way back before planning body
item.description: One of two proposed apartment complexes on Airport Way between Louise Avenue and Yosemite Avenue is back before the Manteca Planning Commission when they meet tonight at 6 p.m.

item.title: GREENHOUSE GAS FEES MAY SHORE UP LEVEES IN DELTA
item.description: Dicey levee stability — a longtime core argument to build a Delta tunnel to help assure water deliveries to 27 million Californians in the aftermath of a catastrophic seismic event — is being targeted in new legislation.
